title: Jean-Paul Sartre — All works
author: Jean-Paul Sartre
current_text: The Vatican offices that published the Index Librorum Prohibitorum banned Jean-Paul Sartre’s complete works as early as 1948; the Index listed books that Catholics should neither own nor read under pain of excommunication. Pope Paul VI abolished the Index Librorum Prohibitorum on 14 June 1966.

sources.quote: One of their last targets was Sartre, whose complete works were banned as early as 1948.
sources.title: Secrets Behind The Forbidden Books - America Magazine

sources.quote: The Vatican offices that published the Index Librorum Prohibitorum, which were active from 1559 until 1966, listed books that Catholics should neither own nor read under pain of excommunication.
sources.title: Secrets Behind The Forbidden Books - America Magazine

sources.quote: The fact that all of his works (both past and any future ones) were placed on the Vatican’s Index Librorum Prohibitorum in 1948 (Cox, 2016, pp. 159-60), was proof, if the censors needed it, of the Frenchman’s degeneracy and bad influence, a justification
'The loss of relevance of the Index in the 21st century' saw it abolished on 14 June 1966, by Pope Paul VI.
sources.title: Heresy, Sedition, Obscenity: The Book Challenged, Special Collections Exhibition, University of Otago Library, Dunedin, New Zealand
